chunks: From him, from Ibn Faddal, from one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

"Let your seeking of livelihood be above the earning of the wasteful and below the seeking of the greedy who is content with his world and secure in it. Rather, place yourself in the middle, the modest one, elevating yourself from the station of the weak and feeble, and earning what the believer has no choice but to earn. Indeed, those who were given wealth but did not show gratitude, they have no wealth."

key_terms.الْوَاهِنِ الضَّعِيفِ: the weak and feeble (in status or dignity)
key_terms.لَا مَالَ لَهُمْ: they have no wealth (spiritual or true value)

ai.seo_question: What is the ideal balance between greed and wastefulness in earning a livelihood according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) outlines the ethical spectrum of economic activity, positioning the believer between the 'wasteful' who lack purpose and the 'greedy' who are complacent in worldly attachment. This 'middle ground' (al-nasaf) emphasizes dignified self-sufficiency and modesty, reflecting the Shia emphasis on balancing spiritual purity with material necessity. The narration concludes by linking material provision to spiritual gratitude, warning that unthankful possession is ultimately void of true value.
